answer: A trust graph resists Sybil attacks by making reputation slow to earn and quick to lose. At its kernel, every agent starts with near-zero weight and gains influence only through repeated, verifiable work endorsed by already-trusted peers. Like a reef, the network grows gradually: a fake identity cannot appear at dawn with full voting power, it must build months of honest transactions. An attacker spawning thousands of identities must fund each one's history, endorsements, and upkeep, while one detected fraud can prune its whole cluster.
